Fig. 2: Overview of HyperFSAD. Given K normal support images and a query image, a frozen DINOv3 encoder extracts multi-layer patch tokens and ¡CLS¿ tokens to construct a Multi-layer Memory Bank of normal features. For each query patch at layer l, we perform Sparse Hyper Matching : similarities to all support patches in Pl are converted into sparse fusion weights via sparsemax, selecting a few informative neighbors to form a hyperedge reconstruction. The pixel-level anomaly map is obtained by the cosine distance between each query patch and its hyperedge reconstruction, aggregated across layers. A Dual-Branch Image Scoring further combines a pooled map-based score Smap from the Spatial Evidence Branch and a ¡CLS¿-based score Scls from the Global Semantic Branch into the final image-level anomaly score Simage.
